title: Doge Goes to Sochi
creator: Dogecoin
deck: A community built around a joke found a very practical reason to send money.
story: Cold light catches the sled as two athletes lean into the push. Around them, the crowd is all colour, flags and encouragement. The illustration makes an online fundraiser physical: many small acts of support gathered at the edge of the ice. The athletes still supply the strength and skill. The people cheering have found a way to help them reach the starting line.

In January 2014, Jamaica had qualified for the Winter Olympics in Sochi, its first bobsleigh appearance since 2002. Qualification settled the sporting question, but the team still needed money for preparations. Supporters turned to crowdfunding, and the appeal travelled beyond the usual sporting circles. A cryptocurrency community with a Shiba Inu mascot was among those who picked it up.

By 20 January, Dogecoin supporters had gathered over 26 million DOGE, initially valued around $25,000, for Jamaica’s bobsled campaign. That contribution joined a wider effort across fundraising platforms. The team later explained that donations would help with training, equipment and shipping the sled to Russia; Olympic organisations were covering airfare and accommodation in the Olympic Village. The useful achievement was shared support for an already qualified team.

The story gave Dogecoin’s playful identity a purpose people could immediately understand. Here was something to do with an internet currency besides watch its price: gather together, contribute what you could and help someone else take part. LORE catches that energy in the moment before the sled moves. The dog on the luggage belongs to the crowd’s story; the competition belongs to the athletes.

details.title: The Shiba on the luggage.
details.text: The sticker on the lower-right case brings back the mascot from 020, Much Wow. It is a deliberate collection callback, not a documented piece of the team’s equipment.

details.title: Sochi 2014.
details.text: The SOCHI 2014 luggage tag fixes the journey in place and time. This invented prop points to the Winter Games; it makes no claim about a race result.

details.title: Jamaica’s colours.
details.text: Black, green and yellow run through the sled, clothing and crowd. They identify the team being supported without presenting the illustrated athletes as portraits of particular competitors.

details.title: A little warmth.
details.text: A mitten in Jamaica’s colours rests on the lower case. It stands for practical help from strangers: an ordinary, fictional object carrying the idea behind many small donations.

source_art_note: Contemporary accounts in [ABC News](https://abcnews.com/m/story?id=21601351), [The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2014/jan/20/jamaican-bobsled-team-raises-dogecoin-winter-olympics) and [Crowdfund Insider](https://www.crowdfundinsider.com/2014/01/30409-jamaican-bobsled-team-going-sochi-coolrunnings2-go/) document the appeal, early Dogecoin total and the team’s explanation of costs. The date marks the fundraising story, not an Olympic race. The trackside gathering and its props are imagined; Dogecoin contributed to a broader campaign and did not pay every expense or determine the sporting outcome. TOGETHER TO SOCHI is editorial copy.

factual_qualifications: 20 January2014 is a fundraiser/reporting milestone, not the date of qualification or the Olympic race.
26million DOGE/$25,000 is an initial reported snapshot; later same-day sources use higher totals. Do not imply a final fixed aggregate.
Dogecoin did not cover every team expense, create qualification or determine athletic achievement.
Card display title is Doge Goes to Sochi, superseding the draft brief’s Doge Goes to the Olympics.
